questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in an english-speaking country in the EU. Furthermore the culture of the destination was very important to me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I got the information i needed for the host university and all communication flowed perfectly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got some help from the International Office at UCC who where very helpful when selecting courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would not say easy. I got recommended through a friend.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive. Everything regarding housing in Ireland is expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The formal applicatiion to the host insitution was very late up until the semester began, and there was not a lot of time to gather info, make the right applications, get a student ID, apply for courses, get rejected from them due to unforeseen circumstances, reapplying etc. But it all worked out in the end. Just a bit stressfull in the beginning.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, the International Office was very helpful with questions, and replied quickly to e-mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes i wanted. However, some were not available to international students. This info was not avaible on the website.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Cast a broad net when selecting courses, and do not "fall in love" with any specific course - it may not be available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses varied greatly, but all felt appropriate for my academic level. All masters level courses were very advanced, and some bachelor level was as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is the same. Lectures and a lot of reading.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sources and Foundations in Environmental Law
International Environmental Law
Introduction to Law of the Sea
Privacy and Data Protection Law
Sports Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Every single one. Especially Sports Law and Introduction to the law of the sea, as the knowledge here was very unique and has wonderful guest lecturers as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The public transportation was very bad, so i bought a bike. it was 50 euros.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was much more expensive than expected. Food and drinks at the bars was cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Uncountable amounts. There over 160 societes and clubs under UCC. There is something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Badminton - great way to meet new people and have fun 
Pub-quiz - same as above
If you are interested in a specific sport and perform at a high level - apply to the club and get irish friends. This is otherwise pretty difficult.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to smaller Irish citites. However, the infrastructure in Ireland is pretty bad, som be sure to plan ahead!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The Irish people are so kind and helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Meet them at clubs (sport) or meet them at pubs. It is hard to socialise in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Pretty much none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness, the enjoyment of their own culture, the humor.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Be sure to have enough money - Ireland is expenvsive
2: Meet as many people as possible - get a network
3: There is stuff going on all the time - if you miss out, there is something new tomorrow - dont worry.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for accomodation as soon as possible.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and learning a lot about my studies and the cultures of the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be away from friends and family back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
